strengths: MSAM offers a simple, practically useful way to reuse momentum for perturbations with one forward/backward pass. Table 1 reports normalized speed of 0.99 versus SAM's 0.52, while improving CIFAR100 WRN-16-4 accuracy from 76.90% to 79.11%.

The evaluation covers several CNNs and vision transformers on CIFAR100 and ImageNet, comparisons with efficient SAM variants, and a small translation experiment. Equal-compute experiments and compatibility with adaptive and BatchNorm-only perturbations strengthen the practical contribution.

The investigation of negative momentum perturbations and their relationship to Nesterov acceleration provides useful insights. Ablations examine perturbation sign, normalization, learning-rate scheduling, momentum, batch size, and alternative directions.

Pseudocode, training settings, hyperparameter scans, uncertainty estimates for CIFAR100, and a code URL support reproducibility. The authors openly acknowledge instability and weaker results on larger ViTs. No material research-ethics concerns are apparent.
weaknesses: The theoretical justification is incorrect as stated. In Appendix A.1, Proposition 1 fails for H = diag(-4,-2), epsilon distributed as N(0,I), and rho = 1: its left side is approximately -0.541, whereas its claimed upper bound is -3. With zero gradient and v = (0,1), Setting 1 is also satisfied. Additional curvature assumptions are therefore necessary. Theorem 3 also lacks an explicit treatment of the required PAC-Bayes assumptions and Taylor remainder, undermining the claim that improved generalization follows theoretically.

The principal ImageNet comparison uses unequal warm-up treatment: MSAM perturbations are disabled during warm-up, while SAM remains active. Table A.2 shows that disabling SAM during warm-up improves accuracy from 69.2% to 69.8%, exceeding MSAM's 69.1%. This known improvement should be incorporated into the main comparisons before claiming comparable accuracy.

Model selection and uncertainty are insufficiently established. Appendix A.15 reports the best perturbation strength from curves labelled test accuracy without specifying an independent selection split. Most ImageNet results use one run; variability estimated from baseline runs on smaller models does not establish uncertainty for SAM/MSAM comparisons. These issues particularly affect small reported differences.

The gradient-similarity analysis in Section 4.2 discards MSAM's component orthogonal to the SAM/SGD plane. Agreement after this projection can coexist with substantial disagreement between the actual gradients. Full-space cosine similarities and residual magnitudes are needed to substantiate the proposed approximation relationship.

The broad claim of SAM-comparable performance needs qualification. MSAM trails SAM by 2.4 percentage points on ViT-S/16 at 300 epochs and 2.0 points on ViT-B/16 at 90 epochs. Equal-compute ImageNet evidence is limited to ViT-S/32, leaving the tradeoff unresolved for the configurations with the largest accuracy gaps.
